## Needs the lead (outside my files)

`new-renderings.md` is now out of step with units.json and must be corrected before its rows go into the table: ἐμμενὲς αἰεί (now "steadily, always" / "unceasingly"; it lists these as avoided); αὖε (now "called to" / "called out to", not "shouted to"); ἔθνος λαῶν `i` (now "the company of the troops"); ἀτρέμας ἔχε `i` (now "stayed motionless", not "stayed still"); add rows for μῆλα "flocks" (table, no departure), δόμοις "house" (table); βριήπυος row should not say "stock". Also, its row for ἀκόντισε cites "the table's ἀκόντισε 'cast' (13.402)"; there is no such table row, the authority is the published 13.402 (iliad-081, "cast with his shining spear"). Nothing wrong with the rendering.

## Flagged items from the drafter — verdicts

- **13.513 grammar.** Source prints ano teleia after ἑόν. Reading kept: μεθ’ ἑόν = after "his own" (his own cast), βέλος the object of ἀλέασθαι. Note already says the grammar is not quite certain and why; no change.
- **13.543 ἑάφθη.** Rare aorist passive of ἅπτω (ἐπεάφθη, tmesis); two feminine subjects, singular verb with the nearer, fine. "fell upon him" with a note that the sense is not certain is honest; no change.
- **13.521 βριήπυος.** Only occurrence; "loud-voiced" rests on βρι- + ἠπύω; note says so (stock-epithet claim removed). **13.475 ἀλέξασθαι.** Aorist infinitive middle with accusative of what is warded off; "defend itself against" is the table's ἀλέξω "defend" (1.590, 13.356); fine.
- **13.467 ἐξενάριξεν.** Table (4.488, 5.151/155, 5.703) is "killed and stripped of his armour" with a person as object; `i` follows it; note truthfully says the stripping of Alcathous is not narrated (13.434–441 is the killing). Kept.
- **13.464–466 γαμβρός.** Checked: Alcathous married Hippodameia, Anchises' eldest daughter (13.427–429), Aeneas is Anchises' son (2.819–820), so Aeneas' sister's husband; "brother-in-law" is right and matches the table's γαμβροῖσι (5.474), not the "son-in-law" of 13.427. (Hippodameia is Aeneas' half-sister, since his mother is Aphrodite; not worth a note.)
- **Cross-references.** 13.93/94 ✓ (iliad-078 ln 91/94); 13.297 ✓ (iliad-080 ln 295 + 2); 11.580 ✓; 11.585 ✓ and 3.32 ✓ (both with κῆρ’ ἀλεείνων, hence the note fix); 11.593 ✓ (iliad-069 ln 592 + 1); 8.559 ✓ line, wording fixed; 5.696 ✓ line, content fixed; 4.186 ✓ (παναίολος of the belt; table 4.186, 4.215); 13.423 ✓ line, wording fixed; 13.404 ✓ (the packet shows the 13.184 unit, but 13.404 is Idomeneus' own and the table row says so); 13.314 ✓ (iliad-080 ln 312 + 2); 13.295 ✓ (iliad-080 ln 295); 2.819–820 ✓; 13.434–441, 13.427–429 ✓; 12.140 / 5.706 / 5.152 / 11.422 (names) ✓.

## Findings considered and refused

- 455 · `n` διάνδιχα μερμήριξεν "same as 1.189": table row (1.189) and rendering identical. Kept.
- 458 · Odyssey line: `i` is exactly the Odyssey's with the colon and the infinitive clause added; `l` likewise. Kept.
- 477 · μήστωρες ἀϋτῆς: table row 4.328 has `l` "counsellors of the battle-cry", but the published 13.93 (iliad-078) has `l` "masters of the battle-cry" and the unit reuses that. Kept (the table row and the shipped line disagree; a matter for the table, not this part).
- 465 · ἀμύνω "defend" vs the table's "ward off": the table's "ward off" is for a thing warded off; with a person in the dative and no thing, 13.312 already ships "to defend". Kept; new-renderings row is right.
- 489 · ἐκέκλετο "called out to" (`l`) / "gave orders to" (`i`): the table's rendering, kept although Aeneas is rallying rather than commanding (as 12.408).
- 493 · γάνυται "delighted" (not γέγηθε "glad"): different verb, rendering deliberate and listed.
- 539 · νεουτάτου: `l` "hand", `i` "arm": χείρ covers both, the note says why. Kept.
- 541 · ἐπορούσας "rushing on" vs 550 "sprang upon him": participle of a different construction; 550 follows the published 11.580 line, 541 the usual "rushed" of the other published occurrences (iliad-020, -031, -066). Kept.
- 513 · `i` "dash after his own": ambiguous English for an ambiguous Greek (ἑόν without its noun); the note says so. Kept.
- 546–548 · δοκεύσας `l` "watching for" vs `i` "having watched": both fit the aorist participle. Kept.
- 514 · ἐπείγετο, 521 · κρατερῇ ὑσμίνῃ, 509 · δολιχόσκιον, 508/520 · ἕλε γαῖαν ἀγοστῷ, 477 · ἀϋτῆς, 496 · ξυστοῖσι, 535 · ποικίλα, 547 · παναίολον, 531 · αἰγυπιός, 538 · τειρόμενον, 497 · κονάβιζε, 473 · οἰοπόλῳ, 470 · τηλύγετον, 493 · κτίλον: all agree with the table rows (5.622, 4.462, 3.346, 11.425, 4.328, 11.565, 3.327, 4.186, 7.59, 5.391, 2.466, Odyssey 11.574, 3.175, 3.196).
